title: Use blind listener judgments alongside audio metrics
summary: Research shows automatic text-to-music metrics can correlate poorly with human preference. Technical fidelity measures alone cannot establish aesthetic success; predeclare listening comparisons.

build.target: Evaluate musical quality by real listening and clearly separate technical compliance from aesthetic preference.
requires: Legally accessible music output or owned clip
Explicit evaluator criteria and permission to collect feedback
outputs: Human preference notes with comparison scope
execute: Verify audio exists and is ready; collect tempo/sections or pitch metrics when supported.
Keep objective checks separate from musical goals such as excitement, beauty or emotional build.
Randomize/blind candidate order when comparing production methods.
Collect listener feedback without inferring psychological state or retaining identity by default.
Report agreement, disagreement, null results and source/model applicability.

applies_when: Aesthetic success matters beyond file validity.
Audio metrics and human judgment disagree.
avoid_when: No consenting listener evaluation is available; report missing judgment.
An automated score is being mistaken for ground truth about preferences.

operator: No unnecessary retention of personal preferences or physiological data.
Do not call listener evaluation 'proven' from a single model-generated adjective.

stop_when: Technical metrics and a separate human evaluation are recorded, or missing evidence clearly noted.

checks: Output contains explicit technical and listening columns.
Blind evaluation protocol and number of listeners are disclosed.
